title: Dog Monday
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: A dog under the table. No introduction. He's there the next day too.

margin.note: A gull with a dog beside it — once. Then never again while the dog lives.

panels.composition: Wood's bedroom, morning. The drawing table. Under it, a low-slung terrier-hound mix, wet, asleep, as if he had always been there. WOOD drawing above him, not remarking.

image.prompt: a young man drawing at a bedroom table with a scruffy low-slung wet terrier-hound mix asleep underneath it as if it had always been there, a towel on the floor, brush-pen black and white
image.notes: The dog is simply there. Do not stage a reveal.

panels.composition: The dog. Folded velvet ears. One eye open.

image.prompt: close-up of a scruffy terrier-hound with folded velvet ears opening one eye

panels.composition: Wood's mother's voice from the door. Wood keeps drawing.

balloons.text: He was behind the bowling alley. Tied to the dumpster. It was freezing.

image.prompt: a young man drawing at a table answering a voice from the doorway without looking up, a dog under the table

panels.composition: The dog's chin now on Wood's slipper. Wood's pen has stopped. He looks down. The panel holds.

image.prompt: close on a dog resting its chin across a young man's slipper under a drawing table, the man's pen stopped, looking down
image.notes: The name is said once, small. The strip never explains it.

art.line: brush-pen now — the weekday deadline teaches the hand to commit; still xeroxed, still black and white
art.paper: the college paper's newsprint; the digest's quarter-letter xerox

notes: The dog arrives. The dumpster from #26. The one time the margin gull has company until 'Lanes'.
